slides.say: A B C is an obtuse triangle, with angle A C B bigger than ninety degrees, and A B is ten centimeters. Which of the following could be its perimeter, in centimeters?
at: A B C is an obtuse triangle

slides.say: We know only one side, so we can't calculate the perimeter exactly. But we can find a number the perimeter must be bigger than, and a number it must be smaller than. [short pause] So this is a minimum and maximum question.
[short pause] Start with the minimum. In any triangle, two sides together are always longer than the third side. So A C plus B C is more than A B, which is ten.
at: So A C plus B C

slides.say: The perimeter is ten, plus A C plus B C. That's ten plus something bigger than ten, so the perimeter is more than twenty. A choice of twenty or less can't be the perimeter. Twenty itself is out.
at: so the perimeter is more than

slides.say: Before we find the maximum, look at the choices that are left, twenty-four, thirty and thirty-five. Only one of them is right. The others are out because they're too big.
at: look at the choices that are left

slides.say: The perimeter can be anything between twenty and some top limit. If thirty-five were inside that range, then twenty-four and thirty, which are between twenty and thirty-five, would be inside it too, and we'd have three right answers. That can't happen. So the right answer has to be the smallest choice above twenty, twenty-four.
at: between twenty and some top limit

slides.say: [pause] Let's check it with an upper bound, one that's enough to rule out the big choices. The angle at C is more than ninety, so it's the biggest angle of the triangle. The longest side is across from the biggest angle, so A B is the longest side.
at: The angle at C is more than
so A B is the longest side

slides.say: So A C is shorter than ten, and B C is shorter than ten. The perimeter is ten, plus less than ten, plus less than ten, so it's less than thirty. Thirty and thirty-five are too big, and only twenty-four is between twenty and thirty. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
